correctness.rationale: Verified unbiasedness by importance-density cancellation of each cell residual r_i=f(x_i+hu)-[(1-u)f(x_i)+uf(x_i+h)] and trapezoidal endpoint integral. For quadratic f, r_i(u)=-a h^2 u(1-u) so its Beta(2,2) density 6u(1-u) makes the random term constant. For C^3 f, dividing the interpolation remainder by q yields -h^2 f_second/12-h^3(1+u) f_third/36+o(h^3) uniformly after endpoint extension; using Var_{Beta(2,2)} U=1/20 gives m^7 Var Q_m -> (1/25920) int_0^1 f_third^2. Independent bounded summands yield the triangular-array Lindeberg CLT for positive asymptotic variance, and Hoeffding with independent cell range width <= M h^4/6 yields 2exp(-72m^7 t^2/M^2). Cauchy–Schwarz forces q=6u(1-u) uniquely among fixed positive densities for pathwise quadratic exactness or universal O(m^-7). Checked uniform-sampling comparator variance 1/720 int f_second^2 under m^5. Exact rational independent moments and cubic variance a^2/(720m^7) match.

value.rationale: An implementable one-interior-sample-per-cell randomized quadrature with guaranteed polynomial annihilation, sharp order-seven variance, a nondegenerate CLT, nonasymptotic concentration, and a precise uniqueness class. The statistical improvement over ordinary independent uniform residual stratification is a motivated accuracy/computational-cost comparison, not an arbitrary moment exercise.

limitations: One-dimensional uniform mesh, one independent Beta(2,2) node per cell, exact endpoint/interior evaluations, C3 integrands.
CLT requires integral of f triple derivative squared >0; zero gives exact lower-order cancellation, not nondegenerate Gaussian.
Exact finite-sample arithmetic is assumed; cancellation near Beta endpoints can cause floating-point ill-conditioning.
